subject.title: Orange — Measure K (Proposed Charter for the City of Orange)

text: Shall the proposed Charter for the City of Orange, establishing the City as a charter city under the California Constitution and providing the City’s governing document for municipal affairs, be adopted?
A “Yes” vote on Measure K approves the proposed Charter and authorizes the City of Orange to become a charter city.
A “No” vote on Measure K rejects the proposed Charter, and the City of Orange would remain a general law city governed by existing state law.

The City Council of the City of Orange is submitting Measure K to the voters for consideration at the November 3, 2026 General Municipal Election. If approved by a majority of the voters, Measure K would adopt the proposed Charter for the City of Orange, changing the City from a general law city to a charter city pursuant to Article XI of the California Constitution. The Charter would become the City’s governing document upon voter approval and filing with the California Secretary of State.

As a general law city, Orange is governed primarily by state law. As a charter city, Orange would continue to be subject to the United States Constitution, the California Constitution, and state law on matters of statewide concern, but would have authority over municipal affairs.

The proposed Charter would retain the City’s Council-Manager form of government and continue governance by an elected Mayor and City Council. It would establish lifetime term limits of two four-year terms for Mayor and three four-year terms for Council Members. These term limits would apply prospectively and would not count terms served before the Charter becomes effective. The Charter also provides that election procedures, district boundaries, qualifications for office, and related election matters will continue to be governed by ordinance and applicable law.

The proposed Charter would permit the City to exercise the authority available to charter cities over municipal contracting and procurement procedures, to the extent permitted by law. It would establish an Open Space Reserve consisting of City-owned properties designated by the City Council and would require voter approval before property may be removed from the Reserve or used for purposes inconsistent with the Charter. The Charter also includes provisions regarding eminent domain, protection of private property rights, vacancies in office, fiscal management, balanced budgets, annual independent audits, and priorities for the use of additional recurring General Fund revenues.

If approved, the Charter would supersede conflicting provisions of general law with respect to municipal affairs to the extent authorized by the California Constitution. On matters of statewide concern, state law would continue to govern. Existing ordinances, resolutions, contracts, rights, obligations, and liabilities would remain in effect unless modified in accordance with the Charter or applicable law.
A “Yes” vote on Measure K approves the proposed Charter and authorizes the City of Orange to become a charter city.
A “No” vote on Measure K rejects the proposed Charter, and the City of Orange would remain a general law city governed by existing state law.
